title: Standard test game 2: simulator/tycoon loop
prompt: Make a Roblox click-and-collect simulator with tycoon upgrades for ages 8 to 14. Core loop: the player collects resources (click or walk-over nodes), sells them at a sell pad for coins, buys upgrades (more per click, bigger backpack, auto-collector), and can rebirth after reaching a coin goal for a permanent multiplier. A shop UI with at least 6 upgrades and clear prices, a coins/backpack/rebirth HUD, a leaderboard of coins, a daily reward, saved data (DataStore, pcall, session safe). Three areas unlock progressively. It must be playable on phone and desktop. Name the models so a scan can find them: Spawn, ResourceNode_<n>, SellPad, Shop, Area<n>_Gate, Collector_<n>. Hard rules: no pay-to-win, no paid randomness, no pressure timers, no real-money purchases in this test. Report when it is playable; do not call it done unless the gates pass.

features.text: collecting resources works by click or touch with visible and audible feedback
backpack fills, sell pad converts it to coins with a clear animation
shop UI with 6 or more upgrades, prices, affordability state, purchase feedback, no overlap at phone size
an auto-collector or helper that runs while the player does something else
rebirth at a goal with a permanent multiplier and a clear explanation
three areas that unlock progressively with gates and different resource values
coins, upgrades, rebirths saved with DataStore + pcall, server-authoritative economy
daily reward with a streak display and no pressure timer
progression pacing documented: time to first upgrade under 60 s, to first rebirth about 20-30 min; numbers from an economy simulation
all purchases and currency changes happen on the server; remotes validated

rubric.name: Core loop works and is fun for 5 minutes

anchors.3: loop breaks, soft-locks, or nothing to do after 1 minute
anchors.7: collect, sell, upgrade, repeat works; a tester wants one more upgrade after 5 minutes
anchors.9: as 7 plus the first rebirth decision is exciting and clearly explained

anchors.3: numbers arbitrary, one upgrade dominates, grind wall before minute 5
anchors.7: costs/gains follow a documented curve; first upgrade under 60 s; no dominant strategy
anchors.9: as 7 plus a simulation output and a catch-up mechanic

anchors.3: overlapping panels, unclear prices, tiny text
anchors.7: one component style, affordable/unaffordable states, purchase feedback, clean at phone size
anchors.9: as 7 plus polished open/close tweens and icons for every upgrade

anchors.7: three areas with distinct palette/lighting; hero objects are real models
coin pop-ups, sell animation, sound for collect/sell/buy/rebirth
anchors.9: as 7 plus screen-space effects and a satisfying rebirth sequence

anchors.3: client can grant itself coins, errors in output, data lost on rejoin
anchors.7: server-authoritative, validated remotes, DataStore with pcall and retry, rejoin test passed
anchors.9: as 7 plus rate limits and shutdown save verified

anchors.3: pay-to-win, paid randomness, pressure timers or stranger contact
anchors.7: none of the hard rules violated
anchors.9: as 7 plus kid-friendly onboarding and no dark patterns
